Title: Diagnosis of test `testLANG571`

Details:
The test `testLANG571` checks the behavior of the method `ArrayUtils.add` when called with a null array and a null element. The expected behavior, as indicated by the test, is that an `IllegalArgumentException` should be thrown when both the array and the element are null.

Analyzing the `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` method:
- The method first determines the class type of the array elements. 
- If the array is not null, it uses the array's class type.
- Else, if the element is not null, it uses the element's class type.
- Otherwise, it defaults to `Object.class`.

With both `array` and `element` being null, the default type becomes `Object.class`.
- The method then calls `copyArrayGrow1(array, type)` where `type` is `Object.class`.

Analyzing the `copyArrayGrow1` method:
- If `array` is not null, it creates a new array with length one greater and copies elements.
- If `array` is null (our case), it creates a new array with length 1 of the type `newArrayComponentType`.

Thus, in our test case:
- `array` is null.
- `element` is null.
- `type` is `Object.class`
- `copyArrayGrow1` creates a new `Object[1]` array.
- The `null` element is inserted at the last position.
- No exception is thrown by the method.

This contradicts the test intent, which expects an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown in this scenario. Hence, the test fails because the method currently allows adding a null element to a null array, resulting in a new array of length 1 with the null element.

The root cause is that `ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)` does not guard against the case where both array and element are null and instead proceeds to create an array of length 1 with the null element, instead of throwing an exception.

Suggested fix locations:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)`

This is where the parameter validation can be introduced to check if both array and element are null and throw `IllegalArgumentException` accordingly.
org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)
